title: Interacting filaments drive vesicle morphogenesis
core_idea: Use theoretical modeling and molecular dynamics simulations to investigate how enclosed, interacting filament loops confined within lipid vesicles—with emphasis on long-range electrostatic inter- and intrafilament interactions and competing filament/membrane deformation energies—govern system-wide morphological transitions; construct morphological phase diagrams for different volume constraints and analyze the role of electrostatic screening to extract design-relevant principles for artificial cellular and soft-robotic systems.
tldr: Explore, via theory and simulations, how interactions among filament loops inside vesicles and membrane mechanics (especially unscreened electrostatics) can organize and control vesicle morphologies as a basis for designing artificial cells and adaptive soft robotics.
